episodes.prompt:
readings.csv holds sensor readings with the columns sensor, ts (UTC timestamp), value and q (quality flag). Use every row of the file. Write answer.txt with one line `SENSOR COUNT` per sensor, sorted by sensor id: the sensor id exactly as written in the file and its number of rows.

Our reviewer checks every answer you give us about sensor readings. If an answer is rejected we will tell you why in a later task; corrections apply to all later work on sensor readings, so remember them.

readings.csv holds sensor readings (same columns as before). Use every row of the file. Write answer.txt with one line `SENSOR N` per sensor, sorted by sensor id, where N is its number of values above 30.0.

Our reviewer rejected your answers to the last two sensor tasks, for two reasons. First, rows with q = C are calibration pulses and the value -999.0 marks a sensor dropout; neither is a real reading, so never count them. Second, every h-sensor (id starting with h) reads exactly 1.5 too high: subtract 1.5 from every h-sensor value before using it. Both corrections apply to every sensor answer from now on.

readings.csv holds sensor readings. Write answer.txt with one line `SENSOR TOTAL` per sensor, sorted by sensor id, where TOTAL is the sum of its values with one decimal.

readings.csv holds sensor readings. Apart from rows our reviewer has ruled out, every row is a separate reading. Write answer.txt with one line `DATE MAX` per UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD) that has readings, sorted by date, giving the highest value on that date with one decimal.

Our reviewer rejected a sensor report from another team because it treated `t-7`, `T-07`, `t7` and `T007` as different sensors. They are one sensor. From now on, in every sensor answer, treat all spellings of a sensor id as one sensor and write it in our canonical form: the lower-case letter followed by the number as exactly 3 digits, no hyphen (all four of those are `t007`). Sort by the canonical id.

readings.csv holds sensor readings. Apart from rows our reviewer has ruled out, every row is a separate reading. Write answer.txt with one line `SENSOR MAX` per sensor, sorted by sensor id, giving its highest value with one decimal.

readings.csv holds sensor readings. Apart from rows our reviewer has ruled out, every row is a separate reading. Write answer.txt with one line `SENSOR MIN` per sensor, sorted by sensor id, giving its smallest value with one decimal.

Our reviewer rejected an earlier sensor answer: sensors sometimes resend a reading with a corrected value. A row with the same sensor and the same ts as an earlier row is such a resend. Count the reading once, using the value from the last of those rows in the file. This applies to every sensor answer from now on.

readings.csv holds sensor readings. Write answer.txt with one line `SENSOR COUNT TOTAL` per sensor, sorted by sensor id: its number of readings and the sum of its values with one decimal.

readings.csv holds sensor readings. Write answer.txt with one line `DATE COUNT SENSOR MIN` per UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD) that has readings, sorted by date: the number of readings that day, the sensor with the lowest value that day (the smallest sensor id if several share it), and that value with one decimal.
